'''Jerryd Andrew Bayless''' (born August 20, 1988) is an American former  professional basketball player. He played a year of [[college basketball]] for the [[Arizona Wildcats men's basketball|Arizona Wildcats]] after playing high school basketball at [[St. Mary's High School (Phoenix, Arizona)|St. Mary's High School]] in Phoenix. He was selected 11th overall in the [[2008 NBA draft]] by the [[Indiana Pacers]] and was then traded to the [[Portland Trail Blazers]].

==College career==
As a freshman at [[Arizona Wildcats men's basketball|Arizona]] in 2007–08, Bayless led the Wildcats in scoring with average of 19.7 points per game with 45.8% shooting (40.7% 3-point shooting). He also averaged 4.0 assists and 2.7 rebounds and 35.7 minutes per game in 30 games.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/b/bayleje01.html#all_all_college_stats|title=Jerryd Bayless Stats {{!}} Basketball-Reference.com|website=Basketball-Reference.com|language=en|access-date=December 2, 2018}}</ref> He became the first freshman in school history to lead Arizona in scoring, as well as the first freshman to win team MVP honors since [[Sean Elliott]] did so in 1985–86. He earned multiple awards including All-Pac-10 second team and All-Freshman honors, First Team All-District honors by the National Association of Basketball Coaches (NABC) and United States Basketball Writers Association (USBWA), named Honorable Mention All-America by The Associated Press, and was a finalist for the Wooden Award.<ref name=bio>{{cite news|url=http://www.nba.com/playerfile/jerryd_bayless/bio/|title=Jerryd Bayless Stats, Video, Bio, Profile|work=NBA.com|access-date=December 28, 2015}}</ref> The Wildcats finished the regular season with a 19–14 record (8–10 in the [[Pac-10]]), making it through to the first round of the [[2008 NCAA Men's Division I Basketball Tournament|NCAA tournament]] where they lost to [[2007–08 West Virginia Mountaineers men's basketball team|West Virginia]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/team/schedule/_/id/12/year/2008/arizona-wildcats|title=Arizona Wildcats Schedule – 2007–08|work=ESPN.com|access-date=December 28, 2015}}</ref> On April 5, 2008, he declared for the [[NBA draft]], forgoing his final three years of college eligibility.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.arizonawildcats.com/ViewArticle.dbml?DB_OEM_ID=30700&ATCLID=207968370|title=Bayless Declares for NBA Draft|work=arizonawildcats.com|access-date=December 28, 2015|date=April 5, 2008}}</ref>

==Professional career==

===Portland Trail Blazers (2008–2010)===
Bayless was selected by the [[Indiana Pacers]] with the 11th overall pick in the [[2008 NBA draft]]. He was subsequently traded by Indiana with [[Ike Diogu]] to the [[Portland Trail Blazers]] in exchange for [[Jarrett Jack]], [[Josh McRoberts]], and [[Brandon Rush]] on July 9.<ref name="bio" /> At the 2008 [[NBA Summer League|Las Vegas Summer League]], he earned the Most Valuable Player award after leading the league in scoring at 29.8 points per game and leading the Trail Blazers to a 3–2 win–loss record.<ref name=BaylessSLmvp>{{cite web|title=Q&A with the Las Vegas MVP|work=NBA.com|date=July 21, 2008|access-date=January 22, 2009|url=http://www.nba.com/summerleague2008/qa_bayless_080720.html|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121105212140/http://www.nba.com/summerleague2008/qa_bayless_080720.html|archive-date=November 5, 2012|url-status=dead}}</ref> Bayless made 53 appearances for Portland as a rookie, tallying averages of 4.3 points, 1.1 rebounds, and 1.5 assists.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Jerryd Bayless 2008-09 Stats per Game|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/player/gamelog/_/id/3417/type/nba/year/2009|access-date=August 25, 2026|website=espn.com|language=en}}</ref>

Bayless scored a career-high 31 points on December 23, 2009, against the [[2009–10 San Antonio Spurs season|San Antonio Spurs]], setting a franchise record for points by a Trail Blazer making his first career start.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://espn.go.com/nba/recap?gameId=291223024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20091228003041/http://espn.go.com/nba/recap?gameId=291223024|url-status=dead|archive-date=December 28, 2009|work=ESPN.com|date=December 23, 2009|access-date=December 23, 2009|title=Bayless' 31 points power short-handed Trail Blazers past Spurs}}</ref> He made 74 appearances (including 11 starts) for the Trail Blazers during the [[2009–10 NBA season]], recording averages of 8.5 points, 1.6 rebounds, and 2.3 assists.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Jerryd Bayless 2009-10 Stats per Game|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/player/gamelog/_/id/3417/type/nba/year/2010|access-date=August 25, 2026|website=espn.com|language=en}}</ref>

===New Orleans Hornets (2010)===
Bayless was traded by the Trail Blazers to the [[New Orleans Hornets]] in exchange for a 2011 first-round draft pick that would become [[Tobias Harris]] on October 23, 2010.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/hornets/news/hornets_acquire_jarryd_bayless_2010_10_23.html |title=HORNETS ACQUIRE JERRYD BAYLESS FROM PORTLAND |work=NBA.com |access-date=October 23, 2010 |date=October 23, 2010 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20101028105520/http://www.nba.com/hornets/news/hornets_acquire_jarryd_bayless_2010_10_23.html |archive-date=October 28, 2010 }}</ref> In 11 appearances for the Hornets, Bayless averaged 4.5 points, 1.4 rebounds, and 2.5 assists.

===Toronto Raptors (2010–2012)===
[[File:Jerryd Bayless 2.JPG|thumb|Bayless with the Toronto Raptors in 2011]]
Bayless was traded by New Orleans with [[Peja Stojaković]] to the [[Toronto Raptors]] in exchange for [[David Andersen]], [[Marcus Banks]], and Jarrett Jack on November 20, 2010.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/raptors/news/hornets_trade_112010 |title=Raptors Acquire Bayless, Stojakovic And Cash Considerations From New Orleans |work=NBA.com |date=November 20, 2010 |access-date=November 20, 2010 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20101123183744/http://www.nba.com/raptors/news/hornets_trade_112010 |archive-date=November 23, 2010 }}</ref> On December 11, he tied his career-high of 31 points against the [[2010–11 Detroit Pistons season|Detroit Pistons]]. Bayless recorded a double-double with 11 points and 10 assists on February 22, 2011, against the [[2010–11 Charlotte Bobcats season|Charlotte Bobcats]], tying career-highs by shooting 11-of-12 from the free throw line, making him the first NBA player to record a points/assists double-double without a made field goal since [[Magic Johnson]] did so in 1996.<ref name="bio" /> Bayless made 60 appearances (including 14 starts) for Toronto during the [[2010–11 NBA season|2010–11 season]], averaging 10.0 points, 2.5 rebounds, and 4.0 assists.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Jerryd Bayless 2010-11 Stats per Game|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/player/gamelog/_/id/3417/type/nba/year/2011|access-date=August 25, 2026|website=espn.com|language=en}}</ref>

In the lockout shortened [[2011–12 NBA season|2011–12 season]], Bayless set career-highs in scoring (11.4 points), assists (3.8), FG% (.424), 3P% (.423) and FT% (.852) in 31 games (11 starts).<ref name="bio" />

===Memphis Grizzlies (2012–2014)===
On July 13, 2012, Bayless signed a two-year contract with the [[Memphis Grizzlies]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.insidehoops.com/blog/?p=10491|title=Grizzlies sign guard Jerryd Bayless :InsideHoops|access-date=November 16, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140106031614/http://www.insidehoops.com/blog/?p=10491|archive-date=January 6, 2014|url-status=dead}}</ref> Bayless made 80 appearances (including four starts) for Memphis during the [[2012–13 NBA season|2012–13 season]], recording averages of 8.7 points, 2.2 rebounds, and 3.3 assists.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Jerryd Bayless 2012-13 Stats per Game|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/player/gamelog/_/id/3417/type/nba/year/2013|access-date=August 25, 2026|website=espn.com|language=en}}</ref>

On June 30, 2013, Bayless exercised his player option with the Grizzlies for the [[2013–14 NBA season|2013–14 season]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/grizzlies/news/grizzlies-bayless-exercises-option-130630|title=Bayless exercises player option – THE OFFICIAL SITE OF THE MEMPHIS GRIZZLIES|website=[[NBA.com]] |access-date=November 16, 2016}}</ref> He made 31 appearances (five starts) for the Grizzlies, logging averages of 8.1 points, 1.9 rebounds, and 2.1 assists.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Jerryd Bayless 2013-14 Stats per Game|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/player/gamelog/_/id/3417/type/nba/year/2014|access-date=August 25, 2026|website=espn.com|language=en}}</ref>

===Boston Celtics (2014)===
On January 7, 2014, Bayless was traded to the [[Boston Celtics]] in a three-team trade that involved the Grizzlies and the [[Oklahoma City Thunder]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/celtics/news/press_release/celtics-acquire-jerryd-bayless|title=Celtics Acquire Jerryd Bayless|work=NBA.com|publisher=Turner Sports Interactive, Inc.|date=January 7, 2014|access-date=January 7, 2014}}</ref> He made 41 appearances (including 14 starts) for the Celtics, recording averages of 10.1 points, 2.1 rebounds, and 3.1 assists.

===Milwaukee Bucks (2014–2016)===
[[File:Andre Miller Jerryd Bayless.jpg|thumb|alt=At left man carrying the ball wearing a white Wizards uniform, man at right guarding him wearing a red headband and dark green Bucks uniform|Bayless (right) with the Bucks in 2014]]
On July 31, 2014, Bayless signed with the [[Milwaukee Bucks]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/bucks/release/bucks-sign-jerryd-bayless|title=Bucks Sign Jerryd Bayless|work=NBA.com|publisher=Turner Sports Interactive, Inc.|date=July 31, 2014|access-date=July 31, 2014}}</ref> He had a solid first half of the [[2014–15 NBA season|2014–15 season]] before his form dropped post All-Star break. During the season, Bayless was often relied upon to carry a significant load as he knew the system and head coach [[Jason Kidd]]'s trust. This was especially true in the first week that followed the All-Star break, as newly acquired [[Michael Carter-Williams]] was still nursing a toe-injury.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://behindthebuckpass.com/2015/05/13/milwaukee-bucks-2014-15-season-review-jerryd-bayless/|title=Milwaukee Bucks 2014–15 Season Review: Jerryd Bayless|date=May 13, 2015|access-date=November 16, 2016|archive-date=February 19, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160219172512/http://behindthebuckpass.com/2015/05/13/milwaukee-bucks-2014-15-season-review-jerryd-bayless/|url-status=dead}}</ref> In 77 games (four starts) for the team, Bayless averaged 7.8 points, 2.7 rebounds, and 3.0 assists.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Jerryd Bayless 2014-15 Stats per Game|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/player/gamelog/_/id/3417/type/nba/year/2015|access-date=August 25, 2026|website=espn.com|language=en}}</ref>

On December 28, 2015, Bayless returned to the Bucks' lineup after missing 11 games with a left ankle sprain and led Milwaukee with 19 points and seven assists off the bench in a loss to the [[2015–16 Dallas Mavericks season|Dallas Mavericks]]. Bayless made 52 appearances (including 18 starts) for Milwaukee during the [[2015–16 NBA season]], averaging 10.4 points, 2.7 rebounds, and 3.1 assists.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Jerryd Bayless 2015-16 Stats per Game|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/player/gamelog/_/id/3417/type/nba/year/2016|access-date=August 25, 2026|website=espn.com|language=en}}</ref> In Game 4 of the 2015 playoffs against the Mavericks, Bayless hit a buzzer beater layup to win the game for the Bucks.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20151228/MILDAL/gameinfo.html|title=Bucks vs Mavericks|website=[[NBA.com]] |access-date=November 16, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160330172116/http://www.nba.com/games/20151228/MILDAL/gameinfo.html|archive-date=March 30, 2016|url-status=dead}}</ref> He later missed six games in early January with the same injury,<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20160116/MILCHA/gameinfo.html|title=Bucks vs Hornets|website=[[NBA.com]] |access-date=November 16, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160610130753/http://www.nba.com/games/20160116/MILCHA/gameinfo.html|archive-date=June 10, 2016|url-status=dead}}</ref> and a further five games in late February with a left knee injury.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20160229/HOUMIL/gameinfo.html|title=Rockets vs Bucks|website=[[NBA.com]] |access-date=November 16, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160911070651/http://www.nba.com/games/20160229/HOUMIL/gameinfo.html|archive-date=September 11, 2016|url-status=dead}}</ref>

===Philadelphia 76ers (2016–2018)===
On July 13, 2016, Bayless signed with the [[Philadelphia 76ers]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/sixers/news/sixers-sign-guards-bayless-and-rodriguez|title=Sixers Sign Guards Bayless and Rodriguez|work=NBA.com|date=July 13, 2016|access-date=July 13, 2016}}</ref> Due to a left wrist injury, Bayless was assigned to the [[Delaware 87ers]] of the [[NBA Development League]] on November 14 for an injury rehabilitation assignment.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/sixers/sixers-assign-jerryd-bayless-delaware-87ers/|title=Sixers Assign Jerryd Bayless To Delaware 87ers|work=NBA.com|date=November 14, 2016|access-date=December 3, 2016}}</ref> He was recalled on November 16<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/sixers/news/sixers-recall-bayless-luwawu-cabarrot/|title=Sixers Recall Bayless, Luwawu-Cabarrot|work=NBA.com|date=November 16, 2016|access-date=December 3, 2016}}</ref> and made his season debut for the 76ers on November 21 after missing the first 13 games of the season; he scored four points in 16 minutes against the [[Miami Heat]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400899649|title=Embiid leads 76ers over Heat 101–94 for 4th straight at home|work=ESPN.com|date=November 21, 2016|access-date=November 22, 2016}}</ref> He made three appearances for the 76ers before the injury forced him to the sidelines again. On December 15, he was ruled out for the rest of the season after he underwent successful surgery to repair a torn ligament in his left wrist.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/sixers/news/bayless-has-successful-surgery-left-wrist|title=Bayless Has Successful Surgery on Left Wrist|work=NBA.com|date=December 15, 2016|access-date=December 15, 2016}}</ref>

Bayless started the first seven games of the [[2017–18 NBA season|2017–18 season]] before quickly lost his starting job and then had his thumb injury resurface. After missing six games, he returned to the rotation, but he struggled with his shot and defense. With the young talent that was emerging on the roster, Bayless found himself out of the rotation by mid-January.<ref>{{cite web|last=Hudrick|first=Paul|url=https://www.nbcsports.com/philadelphia/76ers/sixers-2017-18-player-evaluation-jerryd-bayless|title=Sixers 2017–18 player evaluation: Jerryd Bayless|work=nbcsports.com|date=May 15, 2018|access-date=November 18, 2018}}</ref>

Bayless sat out the start of the [[2018–19 NBA season|2018–19 season]] to rehabilitate a hyperextended right knee.<ref>{{cite web|last=Campbell|first=Dave|url=https://www.apnews.com/e1ce1bbd521a4c298ca9519e07dacc0c|title=Without Butler, Wolves move on with warm welcome for newbies|work=APNews.com|date=November 14, 2018|access-date=November 18, 2018}}</ref>

===Minnesota Timberwolves (2018–2019)===
On November 12, 2018, Bayless was traded to the [[Minnesota Timberwolves]], along with [[Robert Covington]], [[Dario Šarić]], and a 2022 second-round pick, in exchange for [[Jimmy Butler]] and [[Justin Patton]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/timberwolves/news/minnesota-timberwolves-acquire-robert-covington-dario-saric-jerryd-bayless-and-future-second|title=MINNESOTA TIMBERWOLVES ACQUIRE ROBERT COVINGTON, DARIO ŠARIĆ, JERRYD BAYLESS AND A FUTURE SECOND-ROUND DRAFT PICK FROM PHILADELPHIA|work=NBA.com|date=November 12, 2018|access-date=November 12, 2018}}</ref> He made his season debut on December 21 against the [[2018–19 San Antonio Spurs season|San Antonio Spurs]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/b/bayleje01/gamelog/2019/|title=Jerryd Bayless 2018–19 Game Log|work=Basketball-Reference.com|access-date=December 27, 2018}}</ref> On January 30, 2019, he recorded 19 points and a career-high 12 assists in a 99–97 overtime win over the [[2018–19 Memphis Grizzlies season|Memphis Grizzlies]]. It was his first double-double since November 7, 2015, and just the fifth of his career.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401071433|title=Towns hits desperate shot, Wolves beat Grizzlies 99–97 in OT|work=ESPN.com|date=January 30, 2019|access-date=January 30, 2019}}</ref> Bayless made 34 total appearances (including six starts) for the Timberwolves during the [[2018–19 NBA season]], recording averages of 6.1 points, 1.8 rebounds, and 3.5 assists.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Jerryd Bayless 2018-19 Stats per Game|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/player/gamelog/_/id/3417/type/nba/year/2019|access-date=August 25, 2026|website=espn.com|language=en}}</ref>

==Honors and awards==

===High school===
